Subject: Follow-up: Vendor questionnaire route options + clarifying asks (SIG vs CAIQ)

Hi Jessica — thanks again for the quick demo and for walking us through Heron Health's priority workflows this morning. Per our call, I wanted to recap the security intake options we discussed and surface a short list of clarifying questions so your GRC team can decide which form (SIG-lite, CAIQ, or a short custom questionnaire) to move forward with.

Recap / recommendation
- Based on the data types you described (PHI in a subset of pipelines, mainly at rest in your EU test region), we typically recommend one of two paths: 1) SIG-lite prefill + SOC 2 artifacts or 2) a CAIQ prefill if your GRC tooling prefers STAR/CAIQ mapping.
- Our suggested default for speed of review: SIG-lite prefill + SOC2 summary + targeted evidence for HIPAA/BAA items. That gets most reviews to a completion in ~5–10 business days. If your vendor program requires CAIQ specifically, we can prefill that too — timeline similar but we may need an extra day to map a couple of architecture items.

Clarifying questions (short):
1) Scope: Is the security review limited to production systems only, or should we include the staging/test environment and analytics pipelines? (helps with evidence selection)
2) BAA: You mentioned HIPAA — do you need a signed BAA before starting the questionnaire, or is execution post-review acceptable?
3) Residency: You noted EU residency for certain datasets. Confirm that the EU residency requirement applies only to stored data for that workload (not telemetry/metrics).
4) SOC 2: Do you need the full Type II report or is a SOC 2 summary + control matrix sufficient for initial approval?
5) GRC tool: If you prefer CAIQ, is there a specific CAIQ version or mapping your tooling requires?
6) Evidence cadence: Any internal deadline for the security team to complete review? (E.g., target PO/contract signature date)

Next steps I propose:
- If you confirm scope and BAA timing, we'll prefill SIG-lite and attach: (1) SOC2 summary, (2) our CAIQ prefill (if requested), and (3) a short architecture diagram focused on dataflow.
- Quick security handoff call between Olga and your security lead — 30 minutes to review evidence owners.

I've attached the SOC2 summary and a short requirements doc so your team can scan while we wait for your answers. If helpful I can schedule the handoff later today or tomorrow morning.

Thanks,

—Stephanie

Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and one request:

Answers:
- Scope: Please include production and staging. Staging has a small mirror of PHI for troubleshooting.
- BAA: We prefer to have the BAA in place before sharing any PHI evidence or staging access.
- SOC 2: Our initial review is fine with a SOC 2 summary + control matrix; we escalate to full Type II only if the control matrix flags gaps.
- GRC tool: We use RiskCloud and prefer CAIQ to be uploaded to the tool for automated mapping.

Request / open item:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will prefill both SIG-lite and CAIQ (so we can try the RiskCloud mapping) and indicate a single point of contact for evidence uploads? If BAA is required first, we'll need to prioritize that — can you send your standard BAA?

If you can send the BAA and the CAIQ prefill, we'll stand up a RiskCloud import and loop in our security lead (cc'd). Happy to do the handoff call as soon as tomorrow morning (PST).

—Jessica

Quick technical notes for the handoff and for RiskCloud mapping — tagging Jessica so you have the details for import: 

1) Encryption / KMS
- Data at rest: all customer data is AES-256 encrypted. For EU-residency workloads we use region-specific KMS keys by default; customers can bring their own key (BYOK) via our KMS integration if required.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern cipher suites.

2) Data separation / staging
- Staging is logically separated; however, because it mirrors subset PHI we treat the environment as in-scope for HIPAA evidence (access controls, account hygiene screenshots, and masking policies will be included).

3) Logs & retention
- Audit logs: 1 year retention by default, exportable; 3–7 year options available for enterprise contracts.

4) Evidence owners
- Olga will own SOC2 artifacts and CAIQ mapping (controls and narratives). I will own the architecture/dataflow diagram and the KMS/ops evidence.

5) Deliverables for the RiskCloud import
- Prefilled CAIQ spreadsheet (attached in the email thread), control narratives for any custom controls, and a short manifest mapping attachment names to CAIQ item ids.

If you want me to drop the CAIQ prefill into a temporary secure Share link or upload into a sandbox RiskCloud instance, say the word and we'll do it after the BAA is signed (per your preference).

—Marcus
